text:
mendes: Heads up — canary hit an OOM at 03:14 UTC after a sustained 600qps run. Not seeing obvious CPU regression, but RSS climbed steadily. Posting quick logs and snapshot requests.

mendes: jemalloc stats from the process (pid 4219) — pasted output below, can someone scan for weird retained/active ratios?
```
=== jemalloc stats ===
allocated: 3.2G
active: 4.8G
metadata: 120M
resident: 5.1G
mapped: 6.0G
retain: 1.8G
threads: 12
--- bins ---
small: alloc 1.2G active 1.5G
large: alloc 2.0G active 3.3G
```

tia: ack, looking. Retain at 1.8G is suspicious. Can you also dump /proc/<pid>/smaps briefly and a pmap? small vs large split suggests fragmentation in large arenas.

mendes: pmap + smaps sent via gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abc123 (contains anonymized smaps). Key snippet: several anonymous mappings ~256MB flagged RW but mostly unused.

sahil: quick question: was this running with prefix cache enabled? Large KV cache can cause page retention even when logically evicted.

mendes: yes — prefix cache = on for this canary. We set cache_size=6GB but workload had short prefixes so effective usage should be ~1.8G. Strange.

kumar: pinging the allocator team — @tia did the jemalloc config change in the last canary? Are we using per-thread arenas or background purging tuned?

tia: we rolled per-thread arenas=NTHREADS a week ago to reduce contention. Background decay is default (jemalloc decay_ms=10s). Could be retaining because of large extents fragmentation. I'll run extents stats.

oom-bot: [alert] OOM at 2026-09-12T03:14:23Z on canary-cluster-7. PID=4219. Heap growth rate +120MB/min in the last 10 minutes.

mendes: ran heaptrack for a 5m reproduction; snapshot file saved at s3://redwood-dev/heaptracks/4219-20260912.htrack. No single large allocation stands out — looks like many mid-sized (64KB-1MB) allocations.

sahil: mid-sized churn + per-thread arenas often causes fragmentation due to different bin sizes being tied to arenas. Maybe try jemalloc opt: lg_dirty_mult or disable per-thread arenas for one canary.

tia: I can spin a canary with MALLOC_CONF="narenas:2,dirty_decay_ms:500,background_thread:true" to force more sharing and faster decay. Want me to try?

mendes: please do. While you spin it up, can someone run `jeprof` or `pprof` on the heap profile to confirm where allocations are coming from? I suspect the KV prefix cache eviction path is racing.

kumar: @tia go ahead. @sahil I can attach heap profiler with `gperftools`/tcmalloc shim for another canary if you think jemalloc changes might hide the issue. Which do you prefer?

sahil: prefer to keep jemalloc earlier so we see same allocator behavior; try jeprof via jemalloc's prof (jemalloc built with prof). If we can't, fallback to heaptrack.

tia: started canary: canary-2 with MALLOC_CONF set. New logs: canary-2 steady at RSS ~3.8G under same load; older canary RSS peaked 5.1G. Early sign looks promising :thumbsup:. I left tracing on.

mendes: nice. Can you also enable `MALLOC_CONF:lg_tcache_max:16` to cap thread cache? That reduces per-thread retained memory for mid-sized objects.

tia: good call — applied `lg_tcache_max:14` (16KB tcache cap). Re-running.

kumar: while that's running, one more data point: `mincore` checks show many pages in those large anonymous mappings are actually resident (not just reserved). So it's likely fragmentation not lazy allocation.

mendes: attaching quick grep of heaptrack top stacks (trimmed):
```
45%  prefix_cache::insert
20%  tokenizer::token_buf_alloc
12%  request::deserialize_temp
```

mendes: prefix_cache::insert churn lines up with the mid-sized allocs. Maybe our cache eviction isn't compacting buffers — we hold slices even after logical removal.

tia: I pushed a small patch to prefix cache to return buffers to a recycle pool instead of free. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/prefix-cache/pull/748 — canary-2 will pick it up if successful.

sahil: patch lgtm; main risk is concurrency overhead. If the recycle pool prevents new allocation churn, fragmentation should drop.

oom-bot: [info] canary-2 trace uploaded to s3://redwood-dev/traces/canary-2/20260912/trace.json

mendes: status after 18min: canary-2 RSS stabilized ~3.7–3.9G and we haven't hit the OOM threshold. This smells like fragmentation + per-thread caches + prefix buffer lifetime.

tia: I'll keep the canary running for 2h. If stable, we can roll the MALLOC_CONF and the buffer recycle change to canaries and then to canary fleet.

kumar: operational notes: for roll we should document the MALLOC_CONF string and include jemalloc stats collection in the canary healthcheck. Add to runbook.

mendes: will add a short runbook snippet. Also linking a quick command set for future triage: `cat /proc/$PID/smaps | awk '/Rss|Size|Private|Referenced/ {print}'`, `jeprof --text /usr/bin/service /tmp/je.prof`, `heaptrack_print`.

sahil: thanks all. Small follow-up: can we add a dashboard panel for retain/active ratio per process? Should help catch slow memory creep before OOM.

mendes: yes — I'll open a dashboard PR after the canary completes. For now, leaving thread open until we have a roll decision. :eyes:
